clue.text: Justice before Bunthorne's man

parts.note: J is the standard abbreviation for Justice, as in a judge's title
ere is a poetic word for before
Bunthorne is the setter, so the setter's own possession is 'my'

explanation.surface: A judge comes first, then the setter introduces a man of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy is a man's first name, and the theme gives three famous holders of it.

clue.text: Tick Kennedy's heart's condition

indicators.note: read as 'has at its heart', so the condition sits in the middle of the Kennedy initials

parts.note: JF are the first two initials of John Fitzgerald Kennedy
if introduces a condition in a sentence

explanation.surface: A medical query about the state of President Kennedy's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick and a jiff are both informal words for a very short moment of time.

clue.text: Stand and deliver here

parts.note: the highwayman's cry is reread as a platform where a speaker stands to deliver a speech

explanation.surface: A highwayman marks the spot for his hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform on which a speaker stands to deliver an address or a conductor directs.

clue.text: They take the 2 during the chairman's rest break

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come in the middle of the chairman's name, as one event within another

parts.note: Chairman Mao, so Mao's, the possessive giving the S

indicators.note: to break the word rest is to smash its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is taken while the chairman pauses for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 2' points to the answer of 2-down, the platform from which a conductor leads the orchestra; Mao was always called the Chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: Conductors are maestros, and they mount the podium or platform to lead an orchestra.

clue.text: Exaltation in study for this 1 across

indicators.note: the birds' name goes inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
an exaltation is the collective noun for a flock of larks

explanation.surface: Rapture found while studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exaltation' looks like a mood, but it is the group word for larks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Clarkson is the television motoring presenter, one of the famous people with this first name.

clue.text: Bar Hugh's utterance on added verisimilitude

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the bar nearest home
the name Hugh spoken sounds like hue, and hue means colour

explanation.surface: A pub remark by someone called Hugh makes a story more convincing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh said out loud is 'hue', a synonym of colour, so this piece takes two steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Local colour is detail of place and custom that adds realism and verisimilitude to writing.

clue.text: Steps taken by gunners holding stink bomb's primer

indicators.note: the gunners' abbreviation contains the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: the primer is the first part, so just the opening letter of bomb

explanation.surface: Artillery soldiers carry a stink bomb's detonator.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhumba is a dance, and a dance is a sequence of steps.

clue.text: Weapon useless at the front?

parts.note: a pistol carried at the hip, playfully imagined as no good on the front line because it hangs at one's flank

explanation.surface: A gun that would be no help in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or other small weapon worn at the side of the body.

clue.text: Toxic element with ie no dummy particles

indicators.note: the words are broken into particles and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisonous substance said to have no fake particles in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neodymium is a metallic chemical element, a rare earth whose compounds are mildly toxic.

clue.text: Archbishop seeking compliments from this 1 across?

definitions.meaning: Geoffrey ... was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1945 to 1961
one who goes fishing for compliments
Jeremy ... is the frog in Beatrix Potter's tale

explanation.surface: A churchman fishing for praise from a man named Jeremy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fisher names an Archbishop, an angler for praise, and Beatrix Potter's frog.

clue.text: Logic duo displayed in volunteer's mission statement

indicators.note: the letters are laid out anew, displayed in a different order

explanation.surface: Two logicians appear in a charity's statement of purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone offering to go on a mission would say they could go, an idiom of volunteering.

clue.text: Our national title holders

parts.note: not champions holding a title, but the national institution that holds a copy of every book title published in the UK

explanation.surface: Britain's reigning sports champions.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's national library, a legal deposit library that keeps a copy of every published book.

clue.text: After which the suspect parts with riches, sadly

definitions.text: After which the suspect parts with riches, sadly

indicators.note: something done sadly is done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A searched suspect sadly loses their valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip search makes a suspect remove clothes and give up anything hidden, valuables included.

clue.text: Scope for working-class entry to this Oxbridge facility?

parts.note: common is an old, snobbish word for working-class
room means scope or space to act

explanation.surface: A plea for widening access to Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope for working-class' is read as one word put for another, then 'entry' asks for the pair written as the name of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge colleges have common rooms, lounges for members.

clue.text: King of century unknown, honour the succession

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Y is an algebra unknown
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
the line is the order of succession to a throne

explanation.surface: A monarch of an unknown age, honouring the line of succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline is the ancient British king in Shakespeare's play of that name.

clue.text: One thousand religious warriors

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
pi is short for pious, so religious

explanation.surface: A thousand devout fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors.

clue.text: Relax with a slender defender

parts.note: lean means thin or slender
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Unwinding with a skinny defender.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean back is to recline and take it easy, an idiom for relaxing.

clue.text: Don't say a word on takeoff

explanation.surface: Keep quiet as the plane leaves the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mime is silent acting, and as a noun an imitation of someone.

clue.text: Corresponds with strikers

definitions.meaning: things struck to make a flame

explanation.surface: A footballer exchanges letters with forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches means agrees with, and matches are struck to light fires.

clue.text: Crieff Blue metathesised for this?

parts.note: swap the opening sounds of Crieff Blue and you get 'brief clue', fitting for this short clue

explanation.surface: A Scottish cheese gets its letters swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping the starting sounds of two words is the device named after Reverend Spooner.

clue.text: Result of bond with Antonio, no merchant

indicators.note: the letters are carried with the words, contained in their run

explanation.surface: Shylock's bond with Antonio, the Merchant of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Antonio's bond with Shylock in The Merchant of Venice; the bond is chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionomer is a polymer formed by ionic bonding.

clue.text: Tips off zealous English users, getting much angst from this figure of speech

indicators.note: the tips of the words are taken off, giving the first letter of each

explanation.surface: Keen English speakers get anxious about a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeugma is a figure of speech in which one word governs two others in different senses.

clue.text: In exerting more dubious pressure at the far crease in this sport?

definitions.text: pressure at the far crease in this sport?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a dubious, unreliable order

explanation.surface: A complaint about unfair pressure on a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on cricket's crease while meaning a crease in clothing ironed in extreme places.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme ironing is a sport where people press laundry in remote places, so pressing out a far-flung crease.

clue.text: Measure against unknown sin

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
v for versus, meaning against
Y is an algebra unknown

explanation.surface: A sin measured against something unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: The author of one roguish novel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

explanation.surface: A writer who produced a roguish novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazuo Ishiguro is the Nobel-winning author of The Remains of the Day.

clue.text: Chap calling for an end to hostilities, this 1 across?

parts.words: calling for an end to hostilities
parts.note: pax is Latin for peace, a schoolchild's cry for a truce
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man calls for a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Paxman is the combative broadcaster, another famous holder of this first name.

clue.text: A news broadcast taking the rap, we hear

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered, so the letters fall in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report blamed, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins the pieces. The definition says rap sounds like 'wrap'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enswathe is to wrap up, and wrap is said the same as rap.

clue.text: Isle in South Tralee's environs

parts.note: Tralee is the county town of Kerry in Ireland, so its surroundings

explanation.surface: An island off the south coast near Tralee.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a small rocky island or reef.
